manual_corrections_to_automatic_flags: Raw short-line coverage undercounts are not actual omissions: P05 as follows.; P08 by training on code [33, 47].; P09 follows.; F06 final nism. are all present and correctly joined downstream.
A 100% reference-character recall for P01/P02/P06/P07 does not mean valid sentences: additional cross-column text makes them materially wrong.
B reports no whole-paragraph omissions, but loses the separate section heading H01; do not call the page complete.
Raw-cell ordering is not the final reading-order criterion; four B document inversions were confirmed against visual column order.
boundaries: Reference metadata correction: P01 starts a complete new paragraph (We are also aware...), while the Introduction section continues from the previous page. The frozen continues_from_previous_page flag is overbroad, is not used by score.py, and does not change source text, paragraph count, ordering or this result. Frozen reference remains unchanged.
P11 intentionally ends with and on this source page and continues on the next page; this is not an extraction omission.
Footnote F05 retains the source typo no a formal consensus; not an OCR mistake.
No new inference or text repair; no post-result threshold, source reference or runner changes.
conclusion: Crop separation eliminates the observed cross-column mixing on this page but does not produce an acceptable complete method. B trades away a section heading and page-number furniture, retains severe first-line OCR damage, and retains a substantive reading-order error. Do not adopt dilation=0 as a production fix.
limitations: One exposed clean raster page, no generalization or throughput claim.
Review of final visible source content is not a validated OCR CER benchmark.
Null reader result does not alone identify detector versus threshold/recognizer internals.
No proposed padding, resizing or alternative-engine change has been run in this review.
